title: docker run
definition: The most common Docker CLI command. It creates a brand new container from a specified image and immediately starts it.
simpleExplanation: The magic button to start an app. It tells Docker: 'Take this blueprint, build a box from it, and turn the box on.'
realWorldExample: Typing `docker run -p 8080:80 nginx`. Docker instantly spins up a live NGINX web server on your computer, accessible on port 8080.

basic: What does the `-d` flag do when using `docker run`?
intermediate: What is the difference between `docker create` and `docker run`?

answers.question: What does -d do?
answers.answer: Detached mode. It starts the container running silently in the background, giving you your terminal prompt back. (Without it, the container's logs take over your screen).

answers.question: Create vs Run?
answers.answer: `docker create` prepares the container but leaves it dormant (Stopped). `docker run` creates the container AND instantly starts it. (`docker run` = `create` + `start`).

tableData.title: Crucial `docker run` Flags
rows: Detached mode. Runs the container safely in the background instead of freezing your terminal.
Port mapping. Maps Port 8080 on your laptop to Port 80 inside the container.
Volume mounting. Maps a folder on your laptop's hard drive directly into the container.
Assigns a custom, human-readable name to the container instead of a random hash.
Environment variables. Passes secret passwords or configs directly into the running container.
